source_record.json.title: Boundary Behavior under Asymptotic Schwarz–Pick Equality
source_record.json.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{D}$ be holomorphic and suppose $\lim_{z\to1}(1-|z|^2)|f'(z)|/(1-|f(z)|^2)=1$. What can be said about the boundary behavior of $f$ at $z=1$?
source_record.json.background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Normal Families and Complex Dynamics (2007), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2007/09, pp. 487--548](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2007/09)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** partially solved

**Assessment.** The condition is governed by boundary Schwarz--Pick and Julia--Caratheodory theory, which gives strong angular boundary conclusions and rigidity in extremal cases. A complete unrestricted description for every approach to the boundary point is not supplied by the standard theorem.

**Sources checked.**

- [original problem report](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2007/09)
- [Schwarz lemma at the boundary](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.1805)
- [hyperbolic distortion at the boundary](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13965)

This is a dated literature triage derived from the supplied OWR curation; verify time-sensitive status and cited claims independently.
